html:
An ambush in September 9 CE in which Germanic tribes led by Arminius destroyed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus in north-west Germany.

Rome was turning the land between the Rhine and the Elbe into a province. Arminius, a Cherusci chief who served as an officer under Varus, told him of a revolt and led his column off its usual route. Strung out on narrow tracks through forest and bog, in heavy rain, the Romans were attacked over several days. Varus killed himself. The legions' eagle standards were taken, and prisoners were sacrificed.

The historian Suetonius says Augustus would bang his head on a door, crying "Quinctilius Varus, give me back my legions!" The numbers of the three lost legions were never used again. Germanicus later recovered two of the eagles.

Rome gave up ruling Germany east of the Rhine. The river became the frontier, later guarded by the Limes Germanicus, and the line between Latin and Germanic Europe has run near it ever since. The battlefield was found in 1987 at Kalkriese, near Osnabrück.
sum: An ambush in September 9 CE in which Germanic tribes led by Arminius destroyed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus in north-west Germany.
